meaning:
βέβηλος, -ον
(βαίνω, whence βηλός, a threshold), [in LXX chiefly for חֹל ;]
1. permitted to be trodden, accessible (see DCG, ii, 422b); hence,
2. (opposite to ἱερός) unhallowed, profane: of things, 1Ti.4:7 6:20, 2Ti.2:16; of men, 1Ti.1:9, Heb.12:16 (cf. κοινός; Cremer, 140).
† (AS)

elsewhere.note: as knowing this, that law is not made for a righteous person, but for the lawless and insubordinate, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane…
But shun empty chatter, for it will go further in ungodliness,
lest there be any sexually immoral person, or profane person, like Esau, who sold his birthright for one meal.
